Looking at this question, I need to recall laboratory evolution experiments involving *Acinetobacter lwoffii* (now more commonly known as *Acinetobacter baumannii*).

There have been notable lab evolution studies with this bacterium under antibiotic selective pressure. One well-known series of experiments involved the serial passage of *Acinetobacter lwoffii* in the presence of meropenem (a carbapenem antibiotic), demonstrating the stepwise evolution of resistance through mutations in porin genes (such as OPRD) and upregulation of beta-lactamase production. This was a significant study in understanding how resistance to "last-resort" antibiotics can rapidly evolve.

[ANSWER]C[/ANSWER]
